JUDGMENT The challenge in this Original Petition is with respect to Ext.P6 order, which dismissed an application for acceptance of additional documents.

Ext .P6 is sought to be reviewed by filing Ext.P8 Safiya Makkar vs State Of Kerala on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/122722063/
2 application, which was also dismissed vide Ext.P10.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Both are under challenge.

2. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner, the second respondent and the learned Government Pleader on behalf of the first respondent.
3.

Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that in respect of a land acquisition of the year 2012,
Ext.P3 award was sought to be relied upon to arrive at correct market price of the property acquired.
However, the said document was produced after commencement of the evidence.

By virtue of Ext.P6, the learned Rehabilitation Resettlement Authority dismissed the said application, on the premise that the same was preferred after closing the evidence and also that the document sought to be produced has no relevance.

According to the learned counsel, an award passed in respect of the same acquisition of the year 2012, in respect of an adjacent land, is quite relevant; and refusal of acceptance of the said evidence is not proper.

4. Per contra, the relief sought for in this original petition is seriously opposed by the learned counsel for the second respondent, who would point out that the market value can be determined by the Collector only by taking resort to the methods provided under Section 26 of the Act.

Section 69 of the Act is also pressed into service, to point out that the scope of interference of the Re-settlement authority is also limited to examine whether the Collector has followed the parameters set out in Section 26 to 30 of the Act.

According to the learned counsel, explanations 1 and 2 will govern the determination of the average sale price and the new document sought to be relied upon would not help in such determination, in the light of explanations 1 and 2 to Section 26 of the said Act.
5. Learned Government Pleader would support the submissions made by the learned counsel for the second respondent.

6. Having heard the learned counsel for the respective parties, this Court is of the opinion that Ext.P3 award cannot be said to be irrelevant, in the context of determining the market value of the acquired land.

This Court notice that the land which is acquired in the instant proceedings, as also the acquisition of land which lead to Ext.P3 award, stem for the same land acquisition proceedings of the year 2012.

It is equally noteworthy that Ext.P3 award is in respect of an adjacent property,
which is also owned by claimant No.1, the first petitioner herein.
In such circumstances, it cannot be held that Ext.P3 award is not relevant.

The contention of the learned counsel for the second respondent that an award of the year 2015 cannot be accepted for reason of the two criteria afore referred, that is to say, the common land acquisition proceedings and the land being adjacent to the land acquired by the present proceeding.
In the circumstances, the matter requires reconsideration.
7. This Original Petition is accordingly allowed.
Exts.P6 and P10 orders are set aside.

The case is remitted to the court below for reconsideration of the determination of the market value, in the context of Section 26(1)(b) of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.
